comparator.name: Health and Society (Bachelor Gezondheid en Maatschappij)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official handbook defines a 180-EC programme: 132 EC of named compulsory study, an 18-EC bachelor thesis and 30 EC of open electives. Current programme material confirms the half-year third-year elective space, health-policy and thesis sequence.
components: Research Methods in the Social Sciences
Global Challenges and Communication in a Changing World
Introduction to Epidemiology and Public Health
Preventing Disease and Improving Population Health
Health Demography and Global Population Transitions
Data Analysis for Health and Society
Literature Reviews for Health and Society
Genuine open elective space in the third year; no minor or course package is invented.

alternatives.label: Population health, behaviour & prevention
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme combines public health, epidemiology, psychology, sociology, economics, prevention, health communication and mixed research methods.
alternatives.concept: A closest feasible programme in population health, behaviour, prevention and policy, combining biomedical foundations with psychology, sociology, economics, communication and empirical research.
progression: Public-health, biology, psychology, sociology, politics, data and research foundations precede health psychology, disease study, prevention, persuasion and policy analysis. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Health inequalities, wellbeing & social policy
alternatives.concept: Develops the evidenced social-policy direction through health inequalities, social determinants, wellbeing, psychology, economics, ethics, organisations and policy analysis.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres social determinants, inequality, psychology, public economics, ethics, policy and health research while retaining biomedical foundations.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes health inequalities, social determinants, wellbeing and public policy the organising priority. It differs from the closest population-health programme by well over four courses and 30 EC.
progression: Sociology, psychology, economics, politics, ethics and methods foundations precede health psychology, public economics, inequality and advanced social-policy study. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Health behaviour, psychology & communication
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines public health and human biology with social and health psychology, behaviour, rhetoric, persuasion, climate communication, ethics and mixed methods.
alternatives.concept: Develops the evidenced healthy-lifestyles and intervention direction through health and social psychology, public health, behaviour research, communication design, persuasion and ethics.
progression: Public-health, life-science, psychology, communication, sociology and data foundations precede health psychology, behaviour-focused persuasion and applied communication. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; six 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes individual and social behaviour, psychology and communication the organising priority. It differs from both other programmes by well over four courses and 30 EC.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Population health, epidemiology, prevention and global health
Health sociology, inequalities, social determinants and community health
Health psychology, lifestyle choices, food behaviour and behaviour change
Health economics, policy, management and healthcare organisations
Statistics, qualitative and quantitative methods, intervention evaluation and independent research
adjacent: Health inequalities, wellbeing and social policy
questions: How do social, behavioural and environmental factors shape population health?
How can evidence-based interventions support healthier choices and communities?
How can policy and organisations reduce health inequalities?

selection.assessment: The closest programme integrates public health, behaviour, prevention and society. Health inequalities/social policy and health behaviour/communication support two further coherent, feasible and pairwise-distinct directions. Production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: WUR offers a dedicated social-scientific health curriculum with sequenced epidemiology, health psychology, intervention design, policy, data analysis and an 18-EC thesis. UCR can combine substantial public health, psychology, sociology, policy and communication, but it does not reproduce that specialist health-and-society sequence course for course.
